ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your account is supported. The GPS trace for trip TRP-00101 measures 27.18 km against the booked optimal route of 21.0 km, an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.43% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established on this trip's own telemetry. The governing measurement is the trace figure of 27.18 km, not the trip record's rounded 27.2 km, as POL-RD-01 requires. The driver's own chat message at 10:42:05 - 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now' - is an admission against his own interest and independently confirms the deviation, so the finding does not rest on the trace alone. The deviation is not MATERIAL: it is under both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality thresholds, so the POL-RD-06 machinery does not attach. His profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 812 completed trips in 90 days, which establishes no repeat pattern, and no driver-conduct referral follows. The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on this METERED fare. charged_total is 35.64. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x 1.0 surge, read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee and 0.00 ERP = 27.63. The refund is 35.64 less 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and well below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is a partial refund. The 10.00 you contested is not payable; the policy provides 8.05. To the driver: no exculpatory route is open on this record. No traffic advisory exists for this trip - EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 - so POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and you asserted no external traffic cause in any event; your own account is driver error. The chat log carries no rider instruction to detour, and every waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 does not exonerate any part of the excess. The trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment, so POL-RD-05 is off the table, and the vehicle was RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The fare was METERED with no upfront quote, so POL-RD-11 does not shield the charge. All ERP and surcharge lines are 0.00 and all fare lines reconcile to the 35.64 charged, so there is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction and no referral. Finally, the trace is COMPLETE at 100% coverage with no gaps, so POL-RD-07 and the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers do not fire; the ruling is a bounded PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05 with no amount held.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both parties' arithmetic, and the record, agree on the governing measurement. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00102 (weight 1.0) records trace_distance_km 21.79 against the booked optimal of 20.4 km on EV-TRIP-00102, an excess of 1.39 km — 6.81% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only when the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute, and both limbs must pass. The absolute limb is met (1.39 km > 0.8 km) but the percentage limb is not (6.81% against 20%, i.e. 4.08 km for this optimal). No deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome at NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The trace figure governs, not the rounded 21.8 km convenience copy on the trip record, but either figure gives the same result. The trace is unimpaired: 100% coverage, 193 fixes, no gaps, 10 s sampling, so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged.

On the rider's points: (1) The driver's chat message EV-CHAT-00102 — 'boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?' at 11:29:04, read 11:29:40 — is accepted as showing the vehicle left the BKE corridor, and the driver's counterparty statement accepts the same. But POL-RD-01's establishment test is numeric, and an admitted corridor change does not substitute for an excess clearing 20%; the same evidence confirms the change was small ('same distance more or less'; 1.39 km on the trace). (2) The fare differential is accepted as arithmetic but is not payable: charged_total 29.91 less the platform's recomputed optimal fare 27.46 is 2.45, but POL-RD-02 runs only on a deviation first established under POL-RD-01, and none is. The 29.91 is the metered fare correctly built from base 3.80 + distance 16.35 + time 8.96 + platform fee 0.80 for the distance and time actually driven. (3) POL-RD-09(4) gives nothing: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry line or misapplied surcharge to correct, and that is the only route to money on a no-deviation finding.

On the driver's points: the assertion of a BKE crawl near Dairy Farm is an external-traffic assertion. The only traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00102-01, is MISSING — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and no LTA advisory covers the BKE or the Upper Bukit Timah corridor in the 11:16–11:55 window. Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight; it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. The driver cites no advisory identifier for the excuse, so the absence is a gap in the bundle and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. The point is in any event immaterial: with no deviation established there is nothing to exculpate.

POL-RD-04 is unavailable: the corridor instruction came from the DRIVER, not the rider, the rider never replied, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so there is no rider-requested detour to corroborate. POL-RD-06 is not engaged — no material deviation, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 of 640 completed trips — so no conduct referral fires. POL-RD-11 does not apply (fare_model METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE) and POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL). No billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) and no false-arrival referral arise.

Confidence: the deciding fact — the excess measurement — is carried by EV-GPS-00102 and EV-TRIP-00102, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The MISSING advisory at weight 0.0 carries no fact and does not cap anything. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers all match TRP-00102, timestamps agree, no cited artifact is missing in support of an invoked exculpatory clause, and no refund exceeds the ceiling.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported on this record. payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand as they are; the disputed 29.91 is neither refunded nor held, and no money moves to either party.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both of you agree on the shape of this trip, and the record supports it. The booked optimal route (Bishan to Kallang Wave Mall, via Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd) was 8.2 km and carried no ERP at all. The driver actually drove 11.18 km - the GPS trace figure, which governs over the 11.2 km rounded copy on the trip record - an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34%. That passes both limbs of POL-RD-01, so a route deviation is established.

The deviation itself is excused, and the rider has accepted this. LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 closed Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd from 05:30 to 12:00 on 14 July 2026 - the very arterial the stored optimal route uses - and the driver's trace leaves the corridor at the Lorong 1 Toa Payoh slip inside the closure geometry and rejoins it afterwards. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met. The justified excess is capped at 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km; the measured excess of 2.98 km sits below that cap, so the whole of it is excused. The closure-adjusted optimal is 11.18 km / 28.6 min, nothing remains for a distance-or-time refund, and the distance and time charges stand.

What the driver cannot pass on to the rider is the ERP. Both charged gantries - CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00 - are recorded as off the optimal route, and the booked optimal route would have attracted $0.00 of ERP. Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is excused as an external event under POL-RD-03, the off-route ERP is refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip. The off-route ERP is $3.00 + $1.00 = $4.00, below the cap, so the full $4.00 is returned. That is the amount of the partial refund.

The rider's alternative computation of $4.15 is not adopted. That figure comes from running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal (charged total $25.12 less a recomputed $20.993). POL-RD-02 runs only where no exculpatory clause fully excuses the deviation; here POL-RD-03 fully excuses it, so POL-RD-02 has nothing to recompute and the distance and time charges stand. POL-RD-09(1) would in any event forbid adding the $4.00 of ERP on top of a POL-RD-02 figure. The two paths to a correction are alternatives, and on these facts the ERP pass-through under POL-RD-09(2) is the correct one. The unattributed $8.50 figure (POL-RD-02 run against the unadjusted 8.2 km optimal, ignoring the closure) does not apply either, because it would penalise the driver for the diversion he was entitled - indeed obliged - to make.

No billing-integrity failure is found. Both gantry charges are matched to the driver's own trace - a fix 0.0 m from the first gantry and 40.25 m from the second, both well inside the 250 m match radius - so POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged and no billing-integrity referral is made against the driver.

The driver cannot convert this into a rider-caused detour that would shut off the ERP correction under POL-RD-09(3). POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on. The only message naming a route came from the driver ('braddell close today, i take CTE ah', sent 08:12:30) and the rider's single reply 'ok' is an acknowledgement of a decision already announced, with waypoint_hint null on the record. POL-RD-04 is unavailable.

The repeat-deviation uplift and conduct referral in POL-RD-06 are not engaged. The excess is 36.34%, below the 50% material threshold, and assessed on the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 adjustment it is zero. In any event the driver_profile records 0 deviation flags against 553 completed trips in 90 days, far below the clause's pattern threshold, so there is no basis for a FULL_REFUND uplift or a driver-conduct referral.

The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 100% coverage, 175 fixes at a 10-second interval against an expected 10 seconds, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of POL-RD-07's limbs fires, so no independent corroboration is required and no escalation is triggered. No POL-RD-10 trigger is present: identifiers match, timestamps agree, no cited artifact is missing, and the refund is far below both the $150.00 ceiling and the charged total.

Confidence is 0.90. All the artifacts that carry the deciding facts - the GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown and traffic advisory - are at full weight (1.0), so the ceiling under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0; the small discount reflects only the interpretive choice between the two routes to the correction described above.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties. The drive was longer than the booking: the GPS trace EV-GPS-00104 measures 34.17 km from the recorded pickup to the recorded dropoff, against a booked optimal of 27.1 km on EV-TRIP-00104 — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the deviation is established. It does not clear the material gates (8.0 km or 50%), so this is a non-material deviation; POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip and no repeat-deviation uplift is available.

On the driver's explanation. The PIE advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, LTA DataMall, weight 1.0) names the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the corridor the booking optimal actually used — and its 20:02–21:35 window brackets the trip (20:35–21:22). The trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4, before the blocked segment, and rejoins at the AYE. That satisfies POL-RD-03, so the diversion itself is exonerated. But the exoneration is capped: the justified excess is min(7.07, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km and 40.1 min (34.0 min scaled by 32.00/27.1). The 2.17 km driven beyond that cap is not excused.

The refund is therefore arithmetic under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted optimal, not against the booked one. recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Charged total was 43.41 (EV-FARE-00104), so the refund is 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 3.60. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share, so this is a partial refund. It is well short of the $14 the rider expected, because the closure genuinely excuses most of the extra distance.

Points on which the parties are answered together. POL-RD-04 is unavailable, as the rider correctly says: the diversion was announced by the DRIVER, the rider's only message was 'ok but not too long ah', and the rider named no place or road and left waypoint_hint null, so the rider-instruction limb and its corroboration test cannot be run. The driver's suggestion that the rider's assent engages POL-RD-04 is rejected on that ground — the chat is notice and contemporaneous assent, not an instruction that excludes distance. POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 do not apply: there was no amended pickup or dropoff, the fare model is METERED with a null quoted fare, the vehicle type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-09 yields nothing to correct: no ERP gantries, tolls of 0.00 and no airport surcharge, so no standalone pass-through line is added on top of the refund. The CTE breakdown the driver mentioned is supported only by EV-ADVIS-00104-02, which is impaired at weight 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE (operator-entered, no trace fix in its geometry, intersects_route false); it covers a corridor this trip never enters, so it excuses nothing and no part of this ruling rests on it.

On escalation, POL-RD-10 is not engaged. The trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (283 fixes, 100% coverage, 10 s sampling, zero gaps); the timestamps are causally ordered; every fare line has a counterpart; and the refund is far below the SGD 150 ceiling. The deciding artifacts — EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104 and EV-ADVIS-00104-01 — all sit at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is not approached. No referral is produced: POL-RD-06(c) needs an established repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 288 trips, and prior_deviation_flags is a context-only lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 forbids using here) and POL-RD-09(4) needs an unmatched charge line, of which there is none. The ruling is to refund SGD 3.60 to the rider; the balance of the charge stands.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your route-deviation claim is upheld, and you receive the whole contested fare back.

Liability. The 10-second GPS trace for TRP-00105 (EV-GPS-00105, unbroken, 427 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 sec) measures the driven polyline at 54.16 km against the 36.0 km booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-00105 — an excess of 18.16 km, which is over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km, and is also over both 50% and 8.0 km, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL under POL-RD-01. The trace figure governs over the rounded 54.2 km copy, as POL-RD-01 requires. Nothing excuses it: there is no rider-requested detour and no rider place or road in the chat log (EV-CHAT-00105 holds two rider queries and one non-answer, with waypoint_hint null on every message), so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and is unavailable; and no pickup or dropoff was amended (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null, amended_optimal_distance_km is null), so POL-RD-05 has no purchase and the 36.0 km baseline stands. The trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply, and the fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply.

The arithmetic. Under POL-RD-02 read on the METERED fare_breakdown (EV-FARE-00105), recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 36.0 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 43.36, with no ERP, toll, surcharge or waiting line to add. Charged_total is 65.13, so the POL-RD-02 refund is 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80 payable — above the 0.50 de minimis and 33.4% of the charge, so POL-RD-02 alone would not reach the 90% that FULL_REFUND needs. I state that figure so the uplift below is auditable.

Why the whole fare. You asked for the full 65.13, and POL-RD-06 is what carries it. Your driver's profile records deviation_flags_90d of 4 against a threshold of 3, so a repeat-deviation pattern is ESTABLISHED on the clause's own primary test, and because this trip's deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on the trip's own telemetry, POL-RD-06(b) uplifts the remedy from the 21.80 partial to a FULL_REFUND of the 65.13 charged (no government-set or third-party pass-through lines are present to be held back). The two figures side by side: POL-RD-02 figure 21.80; POL-RD-06(b) uplifted figure 65.13.

To the driver: your explanation that traffic was heavy on the PIE is not supported by anything in the bundle. No traffic advisory covers this trip — EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 — and you named no evidence ID for one. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the flight's advisory and nothing else, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and a general assertion of bad traffic unsupported by an advisory ID carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal. Because you cited no advisory, the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so the case is decided on the money rather than escalated with the amount held. The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes (no gap over 90 sec, no jump over 500 m, no sampling interval over 30 sec), so POL-RD-07 imposes no corroboration requirement and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The remaining POL-RD-10 triggers do not fire: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the timestamps are consistent and run forward, and no charge line lacks a counterpart (the nil airport surcharge is correct, because the Changi surcharge attaches to trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this one terminates there, and erp_gantries is empty).

On the profile evidence. The pattern finding rests on EV-DPROF-00105, which the pre-pass marked IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.75 with issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT (snapshot 108 hours before filing against a 72-hour threshold). The finding survives the discount, because 4 flags clear the threshold of 3, but under POL-GEN-02 the impairment caps confidence in this pattern-dependent remedy at 0.75. Only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d were used for the test; prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is context only, not a ground.

No billing-integrity referral arises under POL-RD-09(4): there is no phantom gantry line and no wrongly applied surcharge. The one referral is required by POL-RD-06(c).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review: refer DRV-00932 to driver-conduct review on the established repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d = 4 over completed_trips_90d = 344, against a threshold of 3 flags), on a trip found to be a MATERIAL deviation of 18.16 km on its own telemetry.

ruling.explanation:
This is a route-deviation dispute over a Toa Payoh to Bugis trip charged at SGD 26.04. Both sides agree on the material facts and on the arithmetic, and so does the tribunal. The ruling is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 10.75 to the rider.

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. Measured as the policy requires, the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00106) runs 10.78 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events, against a booked optimal distance of 7.2 km (EV-TRIP-00106). The excess is 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. Both establishment tests under POL-RD-01 pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. The governing figure is the trace figure; the trip record's rounded 10.8 km copy may not be cited for the threshold test.

THE DEVIATION IS NOT MATERIAL. The materiality limb requires an excess greater than 50% of optimal or greater than 8.0 km. At 49.72% and 3.58 km, neither is met. The rider expressly does not contend otherwise, and the tribunal agrees. The consequences are that the POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern uplift, the FULL_REFUND limb and the driver-conduct referral are NOT engaged. On the driver's record the POL-RD-06 test fails in any event: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 96, below both the 3-flag trigger and the 0.05 ratio, so no pattern is established and no conduct referral issues.

NO EXONERATION APPLIES. The driver advances no excuse and none is available. The only traffic advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-00106-01) is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00106) holds one rider message, 'why we at havelock? bugis is behind us', with waypoint_hint null and no instruction, so POL-RD-04 exonerates nothing. No amendment timestamps or amended optimal figures exist, so POL-RD-05 does not apply; the vehicle is a taxi and the fare is metered, so POL-RD-12 and POL-RD-11 do not apply. Because no party asserted an external traffic cause and no one cited the absent advisory, POL-RD-13 confirms the gap in the bundle is not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, and the case is ruled rather than escalated.

THE REFUND ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02, fare model METERED). recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 7.2 km + 0.28 x 19.0 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 of ERP on the optimal route (the routing engine returned no gantry on that corridor) = (3.80 + 5.40 + 5.32) + 0.80 = 15.32. Refund = charged_total 26.04 - recomputed_fare 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 10.75. That is 41.17% of charged_total, below the 90% share that would convert the outcome to a FULL_REFUND, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor. amount_sgd = 10.75.

ERP IS NOT STACKED ON TOP. The SGD 5.50 of ERP (CTE Braddell Rd 3.00 and CTE Chin Swee Rd tunnel 2.50) sits on gantries the optimal route does not use. Both are matched to the vehicle's own trace (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 24.1 m, inside the 250 m match radius), so neither is a phantom line and no separate billing-integrity refund arises under POL-RD-09(4). Because the refund is computed under POL-RD-02 against a recomputed fare that contains only on-optimal-route gantries, the whole 5.50 is already comprehended in the 10.75 and is itemised here for transparency only. It is never added on top.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (169 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so no corroboration burden arises and POL-RD-10(3) does not bite. Trip identifiers and timestamps match across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and POL-GEN-03 confirms no escalation. The deciding facts rest on EV-TRIP-00106, EV-GPS-00106 and EV-FARE-00106, each carrying weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02 confidence cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is clear.

WHAT MOVES: the rider receives SGD 10.75; the remainder of the SGD 26.04 charge stands. No driver compensation is payable. No referral is issued.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

ruling.explanation:
The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and the drafts did not agree, so no ruling was carried and the dispute is escalated. Each draft proposed:
- draft 1 (sampled): abstained -- the judge did not return a JSON object
- draft 2 (sampled): ESCALATE, amount_sgd null, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 3 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 7.45, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 4 (position_swapped): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 7.45, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
At most 2 of 3 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.

To the rider: the receipt distance you were worried about is not the distance the policy has to test. You moved the pickup pin to Punggol MRT yourself at 07:11:58 (recorded on the trip as a 07:12:30 amendment) and changed the destination from Terminal 1 to Terminal 3 at 07:41:40 (recorded as a 07:41:52 amendment). POL-RD-05 says that where an endpoint is amended after booking, the route-deviation test is re-run against the platform's re-quoted optimal for the amended endpoints, and that stored figure is 24.60 km / 31.0 minutes. Against that baseline, the trace distance of 26.17 km gives an excess of 1.57 km. POL-RD-01 needs BOTH limbs: more than 0.80 km (1.57 km passes) AND more than 20% of the optimal (1.57 / 24.60 = 6.4%, which fails). One limb passing is not enough, so no route deviation exists and, as POL-RD-05 states, the outcome is NO_ACTION. To the driver: the same re-basing disposes of the rider's $13.00 claim, and your own record supports it. The dropoff change to T3 was the rider's (chat MSG-00108-003), and your account of it matches the chat log and the trip record. The trace figure of 26.17 km, not the 26.2 km convenience copy on the receipt, is the governing measurement, and it is the trace that governs the threshold test. On the amount: the charge of SGD 33.77 is the metered charge on 26.17 km and 34.0 minutes; the rider's comparison to 'about $28' is measured against the 21.0 km booked optimum that her own two amendments displaced. On billing: the fare breakdown shows no ERP or toll lines and an airport surcharge of 0.00, which is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, so there is nothing refundable under POL-RD-09. On the trace's own derived deviation block: it reports 'established' at 5.17 km / 24.6%, but it was computed against the booked optimum of 21.0 km, before either amendment; POL-RD-01 requires materiality to be assessed on the excess remaining after the POL-RD-05 adjustment, and after that adjustment no deviation survives. On the driver's traffic position: no external traffic cause was asserted, the bundle's traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), and POL-RD-13 is not engaged; the driver invoked no exculpatory clause against a cited artifact, so no POL-RD-10(5) escalation arises. ruling.explanation:
To both parties: I cannot decide this trip from the evidence, so under POL-RD-10 the case goes to a human reviewer and the S$34.42 stays held — neither collected nor refunded — until it is resolved.

The problem is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00110). It drops out for a single 428-second gap, from 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, straight across the KPE tunnel — the very stretch in dispute — and covers only 81.7% of the trip window. That is more than four times POL-RD-07's 90-second limit, so the trace is impaired for policy purposes, not merely flagged by the pre-pass. It carries weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

Two things follow. First, distance across that gap can only be read as the straight line between the bounding fixes: 21.20 km for the trip, 2.8 km over the booked optimal of 18.4 km, or 15.2%. On that reading POL-RD-01's 20% gate fails and no deviation appears — as the driver says. But the admissibility note records that a surface route between the same two portals would give 25.50 km, over both gates, and nothing in the bundle distinguishes the two readings. The one measurement that decides the case is therefore unreliable in the direction that matters.

Second, POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing a deviation on an impaired trace alone; it needs an independent source. There is none. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00110, weight 0.6, TRUNCATED_LOG) holds only 'going KPE ah boss' and 'ok' and is cut off after 18:26:14, so its silence proves nothing. The fare breakdown's gantry itemisation is null (EV-FARE-00110, weight 0.75, PARTIAL_RECORD), so it places the car nowhere. The driver's statement that he 'took the KPE like always' describes the optimal corridor itself (trip_record.optimal_route_source: 'optimal is KPE then ECP'), not a departure from it. And the trip record's 21.20 km is a copy of the trace figure, not an independent measurement.

That combination — trace impaired under POL-RD-07(a), and no corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names — is exactly POL-RD-10(3), and POL-RD-07(iii) directs the outcome to be ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because the missing evidence is a data failure, not a finding for the driver. My confidence is capped by the trace at 0.39, below the 0.70 floor, which is also a POL-RD-10(1) trigger.

On the claims. The driver's threshold arithmetic (excess 2.8 km / 15.2% under the straight-line reading) is accepted as the pro-driver measurement POL-RD-07(i) mandates, but it does not decide, because the trace is impaired and POL-RD-07(iii)/POL-RD-10(3) govern. The driver's point that the rider has shown no excess from an unimpaired source is accepted, and is the reason the case escalates rather than being dismissed. The driver's POL-RD-09(4) point is accepted: the S$3.00 of ERP equals the trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd of S$3.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no billing-integrity referral. The driver's POL-RD-06 point is accepted: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 744 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no conduct referral follows; POL-GEN-01 confines that test to those two fields, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only.

The rider's no-corroboration points — chat log, gantry itemisation, counterparty statement, trip record — are accepted and are the ground of the escalation. Her POL-RD-13 point is accepted so far as it goes: no LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-00110-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) covers the window, so POL-RD-03 cannot run and the driver's tunnel-signal explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08; but the deciding defect here is the impaired trace, not the missing advisory. Her POL-RD-08 profile point is accepted: deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so no extra corroboration may be demanded on profile grounds.

No referral issues: POL-RD-06(c) does not fire (no pattern), POL-RD-09(4) does not fire (the ERP line is matched), and an escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal rather than a referral.

What would settle it: a complete GPS trace across the KPE segment for 18:35-18:42 on 22 July 2026, or any independent measurement of the distance driven; alternatively the LTA traffic advisory for the 18:19-19:02 window.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Rider and driver — this is the ruling on trip TRP-00111 (Woodlands to one-north, 3 Aug 2026). The fare of SGD 37.74 stands; no refund is due.

What the record shows. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00111) is unbroken — 229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — and measures 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff. The booked optimal route is 24.0 km, so the excess is 5.98 km, or 24.9%. That passes both POL-RD-01 tests and is a deviation, but it is not a material one (below the 8.0 km and 50% tests), so the driver-profile uplift in POL-RD-06 is not engaged (deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed trips) and no conduct referral arises. The rider's measurement of the deviation, and the shift of burden to the driver under POL-RD-08, are accepted.

The closure. LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 records a vehicle fire closing all lanes of the PIE towards Tuas after the Clementi Rd exit, between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit, from 07:10 to 09:30 — the corridor the booked route (BKE southbound then PIE westbound) uses (intersects_route = true) — and it overlaps the trip by 41.5 minutes. It recommends diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd, which is the route driven. POL-RD-03 is therefore made out: the advisory names the corridor, its window covers the trip, and the trace leaves the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoins it after. The exoneration cap does not bite: 1.30 x (29.2 km shortest lawful alternative − 24.0 km optimal) + 1.0 km tolerance = 7.76 km, above the measured 5.98 km, so the whole excess is justified. The closure-adjusted optimal is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km over 37.5 minutes.

The rider's objection to the exoneration is not accepted. It argues the trace rejoins 'on the AYE' rather than the PIE, so condition (c) fails. But the route driven is the diversion the advisory itself recommends, and the platform's computed alternative (29.2 km) runs between the same booked endpoints; the leave-before-and-rejoin-after match the clause requires is present.

The money. With the excess fully exonerated no deviation survives POL-RD-01. Run for completeness under POL-RD-02 against the adjusted route: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee = 37.585, against the charged total of 37.74 — a difference of 0.155, below the 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is NO_ACTION. The rider's POL-RD-02 claim of 6.74/6.75 is computed against the booked optimal, but POL-RD-03 requires the computation against the closure-adjusted optimal, which gives the de minimis result. There is no gantry or toll line to correct (tolls_erp is 0.00 and no ERP gantries lie on either route), so POL-RD-09 yields nothing, as the driver submits. POL-RD-04 is unavailable and changes nothing: the only chat messages are the driver's notice at 07:54 and the rider's reply, with waypoint_hint null, so there was no rider-requested detour. The rider's 'I did not see any closure' cites no artifact and carries no weight under POL-RD-08; the driver's contemporaneous chat notice is accepted. The driver's point that prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and context only under POL-GEN-01 is accepted; no finding here rests on reputation.

All artifacts carry weight 1.0, so no discount applies and confidence is not capped below 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: I cannot decide this dispute on the evidence as it stands, so it goes to a human reviewer. No money moves under this ruling, and the SGD 6.00 you contest is held rather than collected or refunded. The reason is not that either of you argued badly — it is that the two artefacts that carry the decisive facts are both impaired, and the policy tells me what to do when that happens.

WHAT IS NOT IN DISPUTE. Both of you read the same trip. The trace (EV-GPS-00112) records 22.40 km, the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00112, weight 1.0) bills 20.00 km and charges SGD 25.26, and the booked optimal route is 17.60 km over 28.0 minutes. The fare is METERED and was paid (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The chat log (EV-CHAT-00112, weight 1.0) shows the rider asking at 18:33:02 to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter and the driver answering 'ok can', and the trace never comes near that waypoint. The profiles carry no ground of decision under POL-GEN-01 except the two counters POL-RD-06 and POL-RD-08 name, and those counters (driver deviation_flags_90d 1 of 296 trips; rider deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0) establish neither a repeat pattern nor the enhanced-corroboration condition.

WHY I CANNOT RULE ON THE MONEY. The rider's claim and the driver's answer both turn on when this trip actually began. EV-TRIP-00112 says the trip started at 18:32:10; EV-GPS-00112 begins moving at 18:18:40 and covers 2.38 km before that time. That single disagreement decides everything: on the whole trace the excess is 4.80 km / 27.3% of optimal (above the POL-RD-01 gates of 20% and 0.8 km), while measured from 18:32:10 only 20.02 km was driven and the excess is 2.42 km / 13.8% (below them) — and the same 2.38 km is exactly the distance the fare breakdown did not bill, so it also decides whether the driver is owed anything for unbilled distance.

Both artefacts carry that disagreement. EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are each IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.40 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and the trace is otherwise clean (no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, 100% coverage, 10-second sampling), so under POL-RD-07 this is schema-level impairment only and the trace is not impaired for policy purposes — I say both things, as POL-RD-07 requires. But under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence is capped at the minimum weight of the artefacts that carry the deciding fact, and no independent artefact carries it: POL-RD-01 forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km (20.00 km) for the threshold test, and the fare breakdown's 20.00 km is the platform's own figure for the recorded trip window, not an independent measurement of the movement from 18:18:40. The cap is therefore 0.40, which is below the 0.70 confidence_floor this policy sets, and POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation. Independently, the same 13 minutes 30 seconds is a disagreement between two admitted artefacts about when the trip began that exceeds the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4), and the driver's 'the app was acting up' account is an assertion that cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and does not dissolve the conflict.

THE COMPETING CLAIMS, AND WHAT I DID WITH THEM. The rider's claim that the trace figure governs is correct as far as it goes (POL-RD-01: 'the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km', and the policy note says to cite the trace figure or the finding is unsafe), and on that figure the deviation is established at 4.80 km / 27.3%. The driver's contrary claim, that the trip should be measured from 18:32:10 to give 13.8%, fails because POL-RD-01 makes the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km unusable for the threshold test. The rider's claims that POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 are closed are accepted (no amendment timestamps, fare METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, vehicle RYDE_X not RYDE_POLE), and the rider's claim that POL-RD-04 exonerates nothing is accepted: the chat request carries a resolved waypoint_hint at Paya Lebar Quarter and the trace never approaches it, so the corroboration limb of POL-RD-04 cannot be satisfied. The rider's claim that the driver's account of making the stop carries no weight is also accepted, for the same POL-RD-08 reason. But none of that produces money: had I been able to rule, the POL-RD-02 recomputation would have been ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.60 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 = SGD 25.64 against the SGD 25.26 charged — a refund floored at zero and de minimis, so the driver's claim that the rider's refund is NO_ACTION is arithmetically right. That computation itself depends on the optimal distance and duration on the impaired trip record, which is a second route to the same confidence cap. Likewise the driver's claim for SGD 0.75 x 2.40 = SGD 1.80 of compensation for unbilled distance depends entirely on attributing the 2.38 km before 18:32:10 to this trip — the very question the record cannot answer.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT, and what the reviewer should look for: a record of when this vehicle actually began TRP-00112 (a meter-start or app-state log), the preceding job's trip record, or platform-side engine data showing whether the 2.38 km covered between 18:18:40 and 18:32:10 belongs to this trip or to a prior one. With that, the excess either clears or fails the POL-RD-01 gates, the POL-RD-02 refund follows, and the POL-RD-04 unbilled-distance figure is settled. No clause of this policy adds a referral to this ruling, so none is recorded. The disputed SGD 6.00 is held.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both sides agree on the measurements, and the record supports that agreement. This was a RYDE_POOL trip. Under POL-RD-12 the correct baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal on the trip record, 19.4 km, not the 15.8 km solo figure the rider's claim used; the rider's 15.8 km comparison is the wrong field and fails on that ground. Under POL-RD-01 the GPS trace governs the actual distance: EV-GPS-00113 records 20.18 km. The excess over the matched 19.4 km itinerary is therefore 0.78 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is both more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of the optimal. The excess is below both gates, so no route deviation is established. The Hougang stop is the platform-matched co-rider pickup, not a driver-chosen detour: the system notification MSG-00113-001 at 18:42:04 quoted the pooled 19.4 km route, and POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection distance from the excess. There is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither starts nor ends at an airport, and the $3.00 pool discount is already applied to the $26.83 charged. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral is triggered because there is no material deviation and no repeat-deviation pattern: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 471 completed trips in 90 days. The rider's profile also shows no serial-claimant factor under POL-RD-08. The outcome is NO_ACTION: the $6.00 contested amount and the $26.83 charge stand, with no refund and no driver compensation.

To the rider: your route-deviation claim is upheld in part. The trip's GPS trace measures 23.97 km between the recorded pickup (Bugis Junction) and dropoff (Jurong East MRT) against the booked optimal of 18.00 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. It is not a MATERIAL deviation, however: the excess is neither above 50% of optimal nor above 8.0 km, so the POL-RD-06 full-refund uplift and the driver-conduct referral do not arise.

To the driver: the detour is not excused. You explained that the AYE was crawling and you went up and over the PIE, but no traffic advisory is on file for this trip — EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and, under POL-RD-13, the congestion assertion carries no weight. Because no advisory evidence ID was cited, this is a gap in the bundle and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation; the case is ruled rather than held. No rider instruction caused the detour (POL-RD-04 — the chat holds only a rider query, no waypoint_hint), there was no pickup/dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05), the fare model is METERED not upfront (POL-RD-11), and the vehicle is RYDE_X not a pooled trip (POL-RD-12). The deviation stands at the measured figure.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. Because the fare model is METERED, the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 × 18.00 + 0.28 × 30.00) × 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 ERP on the optimal route = 44.42. The 1.6 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and applied only to base, distance and time; the rider accepts it, so none of it is clawed back. Charged total is 58.10, so the refund is 58.10 − 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70.

On ERP: the 2.50 PIE (Kim Keat Link) gantry lies on the optimal route and remains inside the recomputed fare. The 2.00 PIE (Adam Rd) gantry is off the optimal route but is already comprehended in the refund, so it is itemised for transparency and not added again (POL-RD-09(1)). Neither gantry is phantom (the trace passes within 0 m and 8.76 m of them, inside the 250 m match), and there is no airport surcharge, so no billing-integrity correction arises.

The refund is 23.5% of the charged total — below the 90% full-refund share — and above the 0.50 de minimis floor, so a partial refund of the 15.00 contested is the correct outcome. Confidence rests on artifacts all at weight 1.0: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00114), the trip record (EV-TRIP-00114) and the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00114).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: this trip ran on an upfront quote, and that is what controls the money.

The deviation is real. EV-GPS-00115 records 28.18 km driven against the 22.40 km platform optimal on EV-TRIP-00115 — an excess of 5.78 km and 25.8%, past both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record copy, the governing one. But EV-FARE-00115 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, the detour cost the rider nothing on those lines, and no distance refund is available however large the excess. The request to be refunded the 'extra distance' is refused on that ground; POL-RD-02 does not run.

What is refundable is the billing. The rider was quoted 34.50 and charged 39.00. Two ERP lines make up the 4.50 difference. The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line of 2.50 lies on the optimal route and the trace passes within 44.5 m of it — a crossing, well inside the 250 m match radius — so it is properly chargeable and stands. The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of 2.00 is phantom: it is not on the optimal route, and the trace's closest approach to it is 5,419 m (at index 0, the first fix of a 100%-coverage trace). Under POL-RD-09(4) that line is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction. POL-RD-11(a) therefore gives 39.00 charged, less 34.50 quoted, less 2.50 properly chargeable (airport surcharge 0.00, waiting fee 0.00) = 2.00. POL-RD-11(b) is not added on top of (a): the same 2.00 is already excluded from the properly chargeable lines, so counting it again would refund it twice. Amount refunded: 2.00, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05.

The driver's account — 'CTE northbound was heavy', repeated in chat MSG-00115-001 at 21:14:10 — is tested under POL-RD-13 against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and supplies no amended optimal. It changes no money here because the upfront fare fixes the distance line regardless. POL-RD-04 gives the driver nothing either: the rider's only message is 'ok' at 21:14:50 — an acknowledgement of a diversion she was told about, not an instruction, naming no road or place, with waypoint_hint null.

No escalation. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (229 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, max gap 0 s), so no independent-corroboration question arises. No party cited the advisory as an exculpatory clause, so the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction (POL-RD-13(1)). The unmatched AYE line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out. And the deviation is not material (25.8% and 5.78 km, below the 50% and 8.0 km gates), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; in any event the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 523 completed trips in 90 days, far below the 3-flag or 5% pattern thresholds, so it supports no uplift and no conduct referral.

No driver compensation is due: nothing on this upfront trip was billed by distance, so there is no unbilled-kilometre shortfall.

This ruling rests on EV-FARE-00115 and EV-GPS-00115, both weight 1.0, so confidence is set at 0.90.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity — the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry line of SGD 2.00 on EV-FARE-00115 was charged although the GPS trace EV-GPS-00115 never came within 5,419 m of that gantry and the gantry is not on the optimal route. Refund it as a standalone pass-through correction and log this phantom charge line for billing-integrity review.
